nodes.label: Backup Freshness Probe workflow
nodes.rationale: Off-host observer: an alert from the backed-up machine cannot fire when that machine or its cron is gone, so silence is detected from CI (TBD-400, INFRA-20, INFRA-30).

nodes.label: keepalive job (re-enable scheduled workflow)
nodes.rationale: GitHub disables scheduled workflows in public repos after 60 days of inactivity; force-enabling each run keeps the alarm alive. Separate job keeps actions:write away from the AWS role.

nodes.label: changes job (pick namespaces touched by push)
nodes.norm_label: changes job (pick namespaces touched by push)

nodes.label: Post-deploy Smoke workflow (INFRA-114)
nodes.rationale: A push to main under an app namespace is a deploy; wait for the new backend tag on the public URL, smoke through Cloudflare, one issue per namespace.

nodes.label: Release Drift Probe workflow (INFRA-38)
nodes.rationale: Flags app releases whose tag in clusters/ lags by more than GRACE_DAYS (Renovate PR open or never opened); reads GitHub releases because GHCR is private.

nodes.label: db-backup CronJob (02:00 UTC)
nodes.rationale: Dump init containers always exit 0 so upload always runs and decides the Job outcome; staging/prod-secondary dumps run under timeout 600 so a hang cannot starve production's upload.

nodes.label: upload.sh
nodes.rationale: One PUT per object because multipart needs kms:Decrypt (denied); manifest uploaded last so the probe only sees complete nights.

nodes.label: tbd.cnf (sized for 640Mi limit)
nodes.rationale: performance_schema off, 128M buffer pool, binlog disabled (no replica), small log buffer and temptable to fit 640Mi; max_connections 80 for TBD pools plus migrate and dump.

nodes.label: default-deny-ingress NetworkPolicy (data)
nodes.rationale: Ingress deny-by-default, egress open for GitHub fetch and S3 uploads; node-local traffic is guarded by DB auth and the NetBird ACL.

nodes.label: postgres NetworkPolicy (ziftbook-staging, ziftbook-prod, db-backup, bootstrap Jobs)
nodes.norm_label: postgres networkpolicy (ziftbook-staging, ziftbook-prod, db-backup, bootstrap jobs)

nodes.label: Postgres 18 StatefulSet (Ziftbook)
nodes.rationale: Sized for 384Mi: shared_buffers 64MB, work_mem 2MB, no parallel workers, max_connections 100 covering staging and production pools.

nodes.label: Valkey 8 StatefulSet (TBD sessions, rate limits, MFA)
nodes.norm_label: valkey 8 statefulset (tbd sessions, rate limits, mfa)

nodes.label: data Namespace (prune disabled)
nodes.rationale: Never pruned by Flux: deleting it would take the database volumes with it.

nodes.label: PriorityClass staging (-100, never preempts)
nodes.rationale: Staging shares the node with prod; negative priority so the kubelet evicts staging first.

nodes.label: IAM role github-actions-backup-probe (list-only)
nodes.rationale: Read-only by construction: s3:ListBucket only, explicit KMS Decrypt deny; trust pinned to refs/heads/main so PRs cannot assume it. Created by terraform/tbd-backups.

nodes.label: Per-prefix minimum dump size floors
nodes.rationale: tbd-mysql=100000, tbd-staging-mysql/ziftbook-postgres/ziftbook-prod-postgres=5000 bytes (~40% of first real dumps).

nodes.label: Backup set manifest (date, tables, SHA256 of dump and grants)
nodes.norm_label: backup set manifest (date, tables, sha256 of dump and grants)

nodes.label: k3s-backup-uploader credentials (backup-s3 Secret, put + KMS encrypt only)
nodes.norm_label: k3s-backup-uploader credentials (backup-s3 secret, put + kms encrypt only)

nodes.label: Pinned bootstrap.sql fetch (ziftbook commit + sha256)
nodes.rationale: Fetched from a pinned public commit and sha256-checked; bump commit and hash (or delete the Job) and Flux recreates it via kustomize force annotation.

nodes.label: Real restore into data StatefulSet (step 6)
nodes.rationale: Restore only into an empty database; suspend Flux and the db-backup CronJob first; gate on table count 0; delete the bootstrap Job so secrets become authoritative again.

nodes.label: Restore drill in scratch namespace (steps 1-5)
nodes.rationale: Run before any one-way door relying on backups and after a backup format change; proves table counts and byte-for-byte INSERT round trip.

nodes.label: Fail closed into the alarm (could-not-run verdict)
nodes.norm_label: fail closed into the alarm (could-not-run verdict)
nodes.rationale: A failed role assumption or listing becomes a could-not-run verdict that opens an issue, because a red scheduled run notifies nobody.

nodes.label: Verified-set .ok upload list
nodes.rationale: A set is uploaded only if its dump verified: exactly dump, grants, manifest with manifest last; anything else counts as missing and fails the Job.

nodes.label: Prod login roles SET ROLE to shared ziftbook roles
nodes.norm_label: prod login roles set role to shared ziftbook roles
nodes.rationale: Migrations hardcode ziftbook_app/ziftbook_migrate and roles are cluster-wide, so ziftbook_prod_app/_migrate are non-inheriting members that SET ROLE at login; CONNECT is revoked from PUBLIC so staging and prod credentials cannot cross.

nodes.label: AOF + noeviction for session store
nodes.rationale: AOF so a restart does not log every user out; noeviction so a full store refuses writes rather than dropping live sessions.

nodes.label: ClusterRoleBinding owner-admin -> cluster-admin
nodes.rationale: Anyone who can create pods or tokens in namespace netbird holds cluster-admin: never grant namespace-scoped rights there.

nodes.label: Deployment netbird (rootless peer platform-node, hostNetwork)
nodes.rationale: Gives owner kubectl access without any public port (INFRA-66); host DNS so break-glass access does not depend on CoreDNS.

nodes.label: Namespace netbird (prune disabled, privileged PSA)
nodes.rationale: Never pruned by Flux: losing the state volume locks the owner out. hostNetwork requires privileged PSA.

nodes.label: ClusterRole alloy (nodes/metrics get only)
nodes.rationale: Only kubelet /metrics/cadvisor, not nodes/proxy which reaches every kubelet API.

nodes.label: DaemonSet alloy (Grafana Alloy collector)
nodes.rationale: One collector (INFRA-85); a DaemonSet so a rollout never runs two copies on the node. Own uid 473 (not nobody) because it sees host /proc environ. Recursive read-only host mounts.

nodes.label: NetworkPolicy alloy (OTLP ingress from app namespaces only)
nodes.norm_label: networkpolicy alloy (otlp ingress from app namespaces only)
nodes.rationale: Only app namespaces (tbd-prod, ziftbook-staging, ziftbook-prod) and the log-retention heartbeat reach 4318; never data. Egress open except IMDS.

nodes.label: Secret grafana-cloud (OTLP endpoint, instance id, token)
nodes.norm_label: secret grafana-cloud (otlp endpoint, instance id, token)

nodes.label: Alloy Kustomization (configMapGenerator alloy-config)
nodes.rationale: Content-hashed ConfigMap name rolls the DaemonSet on config change (Alloy does not reload). grafana-cloud Secret kept outside so a missing Secret only blocks the Alloy pod, not the flux-system build.

nodes.label: CronJob log-retention (hourly, deletes logs older than 6 days)
nodes.norm_label: cronjob log-retention (hourly, deletes logs older than 6 days)
nodes.rationale: INFRA-130: keeps the privacy policy's 'up to 7 days' for request logs; root because log files are root-owned; single node so a CronJob suffices.

nodes.label: Deployment backend (TBD API, tbd-prod)
nodes.rationale: Recreate: no surge pod, so rollout never exceeds quota or opens a second DB pool. Scheduler disabled here (runs in scheduler.yaml).

nodes.label: Init container migrate (alembic upgrade head)
nodes.rationale: Runs before every start so a new version never serves on an old schema; a versioned Job cannot work under Flux. Alembic takes a MySQL GET_LOCK (INFRA-83) so a second migrator waits.

nodes.label: Deployment frontend (TBD Next.js, tbd-prod)
nodes.rationale: Runtime-only config since INFRA-40 (TBD_* read per request).

nodes.label: IngressRoute app (app.thebetterdecision.com)
nodes.rationale: /api, /health, /ready to backend; everything else to frontend; longer rule wins.

nodes.label: Deployment scheduler (TBD backend image, SCHEDULER_ENABLED=true)
nodes.rationale: Exactly one pod: Recreate and replicas 1, plus a Redis lock as second line of defence. Does not migrate; no CLIENT_IP_HEADER since no route reaches it.

nodes.label: Deployment backend (TBD API, tbd-staging)
nodes.rationale: tbd-prod backend with staging values; APP_ENV stays production so migrations and validators run as in prod. Own Turnstile widget so public test keys cannot script sign-ups.

nodes.label: Deployment valkey (staging-only Valkey 8, no persistence)
nodes.rationale: Not data/valkey: Valkey 8 cannot limit a password to one DB index, so sharing would let staging read or flush prod sessions. noeviction so a full store refuses writes rather than dropping sessions.

nodes.label: IngressRoute ping (ping.thebetterdecision.com/ping)
nodes.rationale: End-to-end check that Cloudflare reaches the node in Full (strict), answered by Traefik itself.

nodes.label: TLSOption default (Authenticated Origin Pulls, RequireAndVerifyClientCert)
nodes.rationale: INFRA-93: only Cloudflare with our zone-level client cert completes TLS. Fails open silently with a second default TLSOption or router-level options; fails closed for every host if origin-pull-ca-<gen> Secret is missing.

nodes.label: TLSStore default (origin-cert, origin-cert-ziftbook)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare Full (strict) requires an Origin CA cert per proxied hostname (INFRA-25); one cert per zone, chosen by SNI.

nodes.label: Cluster access runbook (kubectl and Flux over NetBird)
nodes.norm_label: cluster access runbook (kubectl and flux over netbird)

nodes.label: kubeconfig setup with tls-server-name kubernetes
nodes.rationale: NetBird hostname is not in the k3s cert; 'kubernetes' is a built-in SAN so k3s needs no change. curl -k TOFU for CA is acceptable because the tunnel authenticates the peer.

nodes.label: NetBird policy owner-to-k3s-api (owner-devices -> k3s, TCP 6443)
nodes.rationale: The policy is the security boundary: NetBird forwards peer-IP traffic to the node loopback, so allow-all would expose kubelet, metrics and Traefik (bypassing Cloudflare).

nodes.label: Setup key enrolment (single-use, SOPS-encrypted)
nodes.rationale: Setup key is single-use; peer identity then lives on the netbird-state volume, so losing it needs a new key encrypted and merged.

nodes.label: 90-day token renew and revoke (delete SA owner-admin)
nodes.norm_label: 90-day token renew and revoke (delete sa owner-admin)
nodes.rationale: Deleting the ServiceAccount revokes every token at once; Flux recreates it.

nodes.label: CLIENT_IP_HEADER=cf-connecting-ip
nodes.rationale: Trustworthy because Cloudflare overwrites the header and Traefik requires our zone's Authenticated Origin Pulls cert, so only our zone reaches the origin (INFRA-83/93/97).

nodes.label: Visual documentation for a layered Terraform monorepo (research)
nodes.norm_label: visual documentation for a layered terraform monorepo (research)

nodes.label: Target architecture (decided 2026-10-01)
nodes.rationale: One Lightsail medium_3_0 single-node k3s with in-cluster databases; no EKS/RDS/ALB/NAT because the cost ceiling is ~$26/mo against limited AWS credits.

nodes.label: tfc-platform-plan OIDC role
nodes.rationale: A speculative plan runs PR code, so it gets only read allow-lists plus a Deny on node access and the backup chain.

nodes.label: S3 bucket tbd-mysql-backups-884686184019 (Object Lock GOVERNANCE)
nodes.rationale: GOVERNANCE mode: a compromised uploader cannot overwrite history, but break-glass can still clean up a mistake.

nodes.label: IAM user k3s-backup-uploader (put-only)
nodes.rationale: Writes ciphertext it cannot read: no GetObject/ListBucket/DeleteObject and an explicit key-policy Deny on kms:Decrypt; its access key is never in TFC state.

nodes.label: Backup KMS CMK (Decrypt denied to uploader)
nodes.norm_label: backup kms cmk (decrypt denied to uploader)

nodes.label: Trust policy add-apply-remove rule
nodes.rationale: A workspace name pinned in an AWS trust policy (tbd-backups) must never be renamed in place: add the new statement, apply, rename, then remove the old one, to avoid locking the workspace out.

nodes.label: Self-authorization hazard (TBD-372)
nodes.rationale: The workspace manages the trust policy that admits it; defended by a CI fence check, prevent_destroy and a plan-time precondition.

nodes.label: Promote a TBD release (staging, then production)
nodes.norm_label: promote a tbd release (staging, then production)

nodes.label: check-prod-tags.py staging-first check
nodes.rationale: Holds a production bump until staging runs the same tag in git; advice, not a lock, since admins and Renovate bypass the ruleset.

nodes.label: Monitoring and alerts (Lightsail alarms, budget, uptime, stale backup)
nodes.norm_label: monitoring and alerts (lightsail alarms, budget, uptime, stale backup)

nodes.label: Uptime alarm emails during a TBD deploy
nodes.norm_label: uptime alarm emails during a tbd deploy

nodes.label: AWS credits (account 884686184019)
nodes.rationale: ~$140 of credits last about five months at ~$26/month; whether they apply to Lightsail is unconfirmed.

nodes.label: Actions secrets and variables rule (INFRA-99)
nodes.rationale: GitHub keeps only pipeline credentials; every runtime value lives under clusters/ as a SOPS Secret or plain env.

nodes.label: Lightsail node platform-node (medium_3_0, k3s)
nodes.rationale: prevent_destroy and ignore user_data because replacing the instance destroys the in-cluster databases.

nodes.label: k3s GOGC=50 (INFRA-80)
nodes.rationale: Lowers k3s RSS from ~846Mi to ~625Mi for a little CPU; hand-set, so lost on reinstall.

nodes.label: k3s node-name pin (/etc/rancher/k3s/config.yaml)
nodes.rationale: local-path volumes are pinned to the node name, so a new instance must keep ip-172-26-3-190.

nodes.label: Node memory check and upsize triggers
nodes.norm_label: node memory check and upsize triggers
nodes.rationale: Upsize to large_3_0 when available memory is under 768Mi, on OOM/eviction/MemoryPressure, or before a workload that would land under 768Mi.

nodes.label: Upsize: snapshot to a larger bundle
nodes.norm_label: upsize: snapshot to a larger bundle

nodes.label: CloudFormation stack platform-node-alarms
nodes.rationale: Lightsail alarms have no Terraform resource, so they live in a CloudFormation stack.

nodes.label: Diagram drift check on graph JSON in CI
nodes.norm_label: diagram drift check on graph json in ci

nodes.label: Plan JSON as diagram input
nodes.rationale: Plan JSON resolves count, for_each, conditionals and modules and can be rendered later without credentials; state files carry secrets.

nodes.label: otel ConfigMap (ziftbook-prod)
nodes.rationale: Traces OFF in production by default (owner ruling 2026-10-06: they cost more compute than metrics); set OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp temporarily to investigate. Metrics always over OTLP, logs stdout only.

nodes.label: worker Deployment (ziftbook-prod)
nodes.rationale: Backend image running `python -m app.worker`, polling Postgres; 90s termination grace lets in-flight jobs finish. Only the worker sends mail.

nodes.label: ziftbook-mailgun Secret (ziftbook-prod)
nodes.rationale: Separate Secret so it can be written with the public SOPS key alone and rotated without touching the ziftbook Secret; optional so the worker runs before the key exists.

nodes.label: otel ConfigMap (ziftbook-staging)
nodes.rationale: Staging forwards metrics and every trace (traffic is tiny); logs stay on stdout.

nodes.label: worker Deployment (ziftbook-staging)
nodes.rationale: Backend image running `python -m app.worker`, polling Postgres; 90s termination grace lets in-flight jobs finish. Only the worker sends mail.

nodes.label: ziftbook-mailgun Secret (ziftbook-staging)
nodes.rationale: Separate Secret so it can be written with the public SOPS key alone and rotated without touching the ziftbook Secret; optional so the worker runs before the key exists.

nodes.label: Renovate image bumps (vX.Y.Z)
nodes.rationale: Renovate bumps frontend, backend and migrations images together; staging automerges (INFRA-36), prod PR is never automerged so merging is the deploy.

nodes.label: Ziftbook Postgres database (job queue and app data)
nodes.norm_label: ziftbook postgres database (job queue and app data)

nodes.label: Alembic migrate-before-start init container pattern
nodes.rationale: `alembic upgrade head` runs before every start (no-op at head, advisory-locked) so a new version never serves on an old schema; backend and worker share it.

nodes.label: Recreate rollout strategy (no surge)
nodes.rationale: No surge pod, so a rollout never exceeds the namespace quota or opens a second DB pool; worker runs one at a time.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-For trust model (ZIF_TRUSTED_PROXIES 10.42.0.0/16)
nodes.rationale: Backend trusts X-Forwarded-For only from the cluster CIDR (not the node podCIDR, which changes on re-register); safe because the NetworkPolicy admits only the frontend, which sets it from cf-connecting-ip. Node-local traffic (10.42.0.1) is owner-only via NetBird.

nodes.label: HCP Terraform workspaces (aws-platform, cloudflare, cloudflare-tokens, tbd-backups)
nodes.norm_label: hcp terraform workspaces (aws-platform, cloudflare, cloudflare-tokens, tbd-backups)

nodes.label: Genesis by root (MFA, break-glass user, roles, workspace)
nodes.norm_label: genesis by root (mfa, break-glass user, roles, workspace)

nodes.label: Run-phase split of TFC OIDC roles
nodes.norm_label: run-phase split of tfc oidc roles
nodes.rationale: HCP Terraform runs a speculative plan on every unapproved PR; one run_phase:* role would let an unmerged PR read production backups, so plan and apply use separate roles and TFC_AWS_RUN_ROLE_ARN is never set.

nodes.label: Grafana Alloy DaemonSet (observability)
nodes.rationale: One collector so Grafana Cloud credentials live in one SOPS Secret; not the k8s-monitoring chart, which deploys several Alloys plus node-exporter and kube-state-metrics.

nodes.label: Grafana Cloud stack, access policy and API-provisioned alerts
nodes.norm_label: grafana cloud stack, access policy and api-provisioned alerts

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry telemetry standard (INFRA-84)
nodes.rationale: Apps own their OTel SDK setup with an attribute allowlist, no exception messages and traceparent only, because url.path/query and error strings can carry invite tokens, OAuth codes and emails. Traces off in production by default since they cost more compute.

nodes.label: Build once, retag (sha-<7> to vX.Y.Z)
nodes.rationale: A release never rebuilds: staging and production run the same image digest.

nodes.label: Instance metadata (169.254.169.254) egress block
nodes.rationale: Egress is open except IMDS; nothing in the namespace needs it (staging images automerge, raising the stakes).

nodes.label: NetworkPolicy egress-no-imds (tbd-prod)
nodes.rationale: Egress open except instance metadata 169.254.169.254.

nodes.label: observability Namespace (privileged, Grafana Alloy)
nodes.rationale: Privileged only because baseline forbids hostPath for node metrics and the log-retention job (INFRA-85, INFRA-130).

nodes.label: kubeconform validation of clusters/ (pinned CRDs-catalog)
nodes.rationale: Flux CRDs come from flux install --export and have no published schema, so CRDs are skipped and Flux CRs validate against a pinned datreeio CRDs-catalog commit; non-strict because SOPS adds a sops: field.

nodes.label: Terraform checks job (fmt, validate, tflint, python tests)
nodes.norm_label: terraform checks job (fmt, validate, tflint, python tests)

nodes.label: Flux v2.9.6 install manifest (source + kustomize controllers only)
nodes.norm_label: flux v2.9.6 install manifest (source + kustomize controllers only)
nodes.rationale: Generated by flux install --export; do not edit, patches go in kustomization.yaml.

nodes.label: age key (private key offline and in-cluster as flux-system/sops-age)
nodes.norm_label: age key (private key offline and in-cluster as flux-system/sops-age)

nodes.label: Flux CRDs (GitRepository, OCIRepository, Bucket, Helm*, Kustomization)
nodes.norm_label: flux crds (gitrepository, ocirepository, bucket, helm*, kustomization)

nodes.label: Controller memory limit patch (256Mi)
nodes.rationale: Upstream 1Gi limits per controller are too large on a 4 GB node where each used ~40Mi (INFRA-80); patched here so gotk-components.yaml can be regenerated.

nodes.label: Cloudflare edge rate limit on auth endpoints (INFRA-123)
nodes.norm_label: cloudflare edge rate limit on auth endpoints (infra-123)
nodes.rationale: Free plan allows one path-only rule per zone; caps one IP at 20 requests/10 s before the app's own limits.

nodes.label: Mailgun EU HTTP API mail standard
nodes.norm_label: mailgun eu http api mail standard
nodes.rationale: No SMTP or in-cluster mail server; dev/staging share m.fjconsulting.dev with a send-only key per environment, production gets m.<appdomain>.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Origin CA certificates (one per zone)
nodes.norm_label: cloudflare origin ca certificates (one per zone)
nodes.rationale: An Origin CA cert covers one zone only, so TLSStore default holds origin-cert and origin-cert-ziftbook and Traefik picks by SNI.

nodes.label: Traefik ingress (TLSStore default, SNI per zone)
nodes.norm_label: traefik ingress (tlsstore default, sni per zone)

nodes.label: Valkey 8 (TBD sessions)
nodes.rationale: Kept only for TBD until INFRA-121/INFRA-122 move its state to MySQL; a shared Valkey is unsafe because ACLs cannot confine KEYS/SCAN/FLUSH and maxmemory/noeviction are instance-wide.

nodes.label: Cloudflare bootstrap token (cloudflare-tokens workspace)
nodes.rationale: The only hand-made Cloudflare token; it can mint any token so it is treated as account admin and held only by that workspace.

nodes.label: Worker and Snippet access (INFRA-98)
nodes.rationale: A Worker on an app zone can forge CF-Connecting-IP towards that zone's node hostnames; deploy tokens are narrowed to one Worker each, the code-level residual is not accepted (INFRA-145).

nodes.label: Add a public hostname for an app
nodes.norm_label: add a public hostname for an app

nodes.label: Write or rotate a Kubernetes Secret
nodes.norm_label: write or rotate a kubernetes secret
nodes.rationale: Encrypting a new file needs only the public key; editing needs the offline private key, so each rotated value gets its own Secret file regenerated whole.

nodes.label: flux-system/sops-age bootstrap secret
nodes.rationale: Typed at a silent prompt with a length guard so the age private key never lands in shell history; apply gotk files, not apply -k, because encrypted Secrets fail kubectl validation.

nodes.label: Jobs, locks, sessions and rate limits in the app database (INFRA-102)
nodes.norm_label: jobs, locks, sessions and rate limits in the app database (infra-102)
nodes.rationale: One failure domain (Valkey timeouts once turned every TBD auth endpoint into a 500), state covered by nightly dumps, no extra pods; works on both MySQL 8.4 and Postgres 18. Ziftbook is the reference implementation.

nodes.label: Authenticated Origin Pulls client certificate (INFRA-93)
nodes.rationale: The firewall admits every Cloudflare IP, so any Cloudflare zone could reach the node; Traefik's TLSOption default requires our own client cert. It fails closed, so Cloudflare must present the cert before the origin requires it, and rotation runs one merge per step.
